mcat_description.short: Prefabricated hospitals are complete modular healthcare facility buildings assembled from factory-manufactured structural components — typically PUF/PUP sandwich panels on steel frames — and erected on-site as temporary or permanent hospital infrastructure.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated hospitals are turnkey modular building systems designed to deliver fully functional healthcare facilities — including OPDs, ICUs, operation theatres, patient wards, diagnostic labs, and support areas — using off-site manufactured components assembled rapidly on-site. Structural systems typically use insulated sandwich panels (PUF/PUP), pre-engineered steel frames, and modular room units that can be configured to any floor plan and expanded over time. In the Indian market, these structures must comply with NABH infrastructure guidelines, the National Building Code (NBC), and relevant BIS structural standards, while supporting MEP integration (HVAC, medical gas pipelines, electrical, plumbing). Key demand drivers include government health infrastructure programmes (Ayushman Bharat, PM-ABHIM), disaster and emergency response deployment, and rapid capacity expansion by private hospital chains in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

market_context: Prefabricated hospitals in India are a fast-growing segment of the modular construction market, driven by government health infrastructure programmes (Ayushman Bharat, PM-ABHIM), disaster response requirements, and private hospital expansion in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. The dominant construction system uses insulated PUF (Polyurethane Foam) or PUP (Polyurethane Panel) sandwich panels on pre-engineered steel frames, enabling 60–70% faster construction than conventional methods. Compliance with NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers) infrastructure guidelines and the National Building Code of India (NBC) are the primary regulatory benchmarks; NABH accreditation is a prerequisite for government empanelment and insurance cashless services. Key Indian manufacturers include Pressmach, EPACK Prefab, and Wedge India; international specialists with Indian operations include KEF-TAHPI (factory near Bangalore). The market distinguishes between full-scale turnkey hospital buildings (multi-specialty, permanent foundation), portable/relocatable hospital units (G+1 PUP structures for remote or emergency use), and modular add-on blocks (ICU wings, OT suites, isolation wards). India's hospital infrastructure market is projected to require over 2 billion sq ft of additional space by 2030, creating sustained demand for prefabricated solutions (single source — Woodkraft/IBEF-cited projection).
